Five versioned task types grade actual artifacts, with observed failures and corrected passes. Parent assertions consume bounded child observations; a claimed success transcript or forged stdout cannot qualify.

Task/grader/controller identity is frozen, extra or missing source and symlinks are refused, runs bind exact graded attempts, and incomparable or stale trials are denied. Tests preserve repeated attempts.

The public CLI prepares and grades operator-edited trials without provider commands or credentials. Deterministic fixture, replay, operator-hosted live and unavailable records are distinct; no live-model performance is claimed.

Actual check timing, retries and review corrections are recorded. Comparable manifests preserve null usage, charge all failures against distinct accepted work, bind source/attempt and separate grading from infrastructure. Tests cover frozen measurements and duplicate outcomes.

Actual fixture reproduces failure, adds an executable repository regression, separately executes the named test red then green with unchanged assertions, verifies and reviews the correction, and closes feedback. An always-passing new test beside an unrelated failure is rejected. Quality references retain explicit environment/assurance.

AGENTS starts and links the local review server. One CLI handles lightweight/roadmap work, qualification, claims, recovery, trials, run comparison and feedback. JSON-only projection, dynamic UI and real Chrome desktop/mobile checks pass.

Security-relevant threat model covers scope, recovery, test/grader substitution, ownership, private output, resource bounds, metadata and feedback. Independent review findings were corrected and denial regressions pass. Existing host permissions, cooperative local integrity and operator attestations remain explicit limits.

Final qualification was executed and reported honestly: focused control-plane tests pass; docs/agent-support/architecture/skill checks pass. npm run test:all is NOT green: standard Node reports 36 failures in unchanged application files; standard Vitest (407) and E2E (91 Node, 3 Vitest) pass. Two controlled AI integrations were skipped. No live-model or whole-repository success claim is made; aggregate logs and reports are retained under artifacts/.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Starting only from AGENTS.md, a future agent can discover the canonical guide and CLI, determine whether a lightweight task or approved roadmap applies, inspect the next legal action, and follow one workflow without discovering a competing planning hierarchy. Natural-language routing and installation tests cover the revised behavior.

New substantial work binds a user or operator outcome, critical journey, observable success and relevant quality constraints to acceptance and scope before implementation. Internal work uses a concrete rationale. Acceptance or policy changes cannot silently weaken the evidence that authorizes the same work.

Reuse suitable generic mechanisms and focused tests from financial-ai-academy revision 8e7ef88de24ef222c8dc3e72a96b76fddc629820 after dependency and license inspection. Preserve applicable notices and record provenance. Keep project-specific CAP/SLI/WRK adapters, approval semantics, browser site, and portfolio UI outside this integration. Where direct copying would introduce incompatible coupling or require an unresolved licensing decision, reuse the design with a documented reason rather than silently changing product licensing.

Each candidate change is classified, including untracked source additions, deletions, and both sides of renames. Mixed classified and unclassified changes fail closed. Selected check IDs, matched paths, deferred checks, plan digest, and policy provenance are deterministic and inspectable. Ordinary internal chunks select focused checks; aggregate suites remain reserved for overall completion.

A real allowlisted check execution produces a receipt with bound source/test inputs, environment and catalog identity, bounded output digests, artifact integrity, exit status, elapsed time, and timeout disposition. Current qualification rejects forged, incomplete, stale, failed, or mismatched evidence. Routine controller-generated report and evidence projections do not create circular invalidation; material source, test, acceptance, or policy changes invalidate the affected evidence.

Substantial governed work needs a separate candidate-bound technical review with explicit invocation provenance and transparent identity assurance. Self-review, stale dispositions, and open blocking findings prevent completion. Substantive corrections receive fresh verification and review; cosmetic observations cannot create arbitrary approval loops. Supplied labels or hashes are never represented as authenticated independent identity.

Concurrent claim and state-publication tests prove scoped single ownership, revision conflicts, exact-file overlap handling, stale-owner rejection, explicit expiry recovery, preserved history, and idempotent interrupted multi-file publication. Read-only inspection acquires no editing ownership. Claims remain cooperative coordination and do not claim to be an operating-system sandbox.

Existing roadmap definitions, approvals, completed history, reports, and supported event flows remain readable and resumable through a documented versioned adoption path. Historical declarations are not retroactively promoted to verified receipts. New governed completion requires current evidence, and the complete outcome-to-correction-to-completion workflow executes successfully through the public CLI in an isolated fixture.

Record the security-relevant design and threat/control mapping for authorization, stale evidence, local process execution, path containment, policy substitution, concurrency, recovery, and privacy. Focused denial, malformed-input, redaction, resource-bound, and failure tests pass. Preserve the external host sandbox and user authority, document local trust limits, and ensure rollback cannot restore unsupported verified completion.

The server and UI dynamically reflect current versioned JSON state without parsing Markdown. A realistic workflow request starting at AGENTS.md starts or safely reuses the correct repository server and provides its verified loopback link. Changed JSON records update the API and browser view without regeneration. Read-only routes reject remote binding, unexpected Host/Origin, writes, path traversal, private files and malformed/oversized inputs without leaking raw errors. Browser and HTTP tests cover accessible navigation, empty/error states and safe untrusted text rendering.

acceptanceCriteria.description: At least five versioned repository-relevant task types have concrete fixtures and independent executable acceptance: defect correction, cross-boundary behavior, a user-facing critical journey, security denial, and decision-gate escalation. The harness grades actual resulting artifacts and behavioral evidence; a scenario transcript claiming success cannot substitute for a successful grader execution.

Trial work cannot silently alter the trusted grader, acceptance, task version, repository/policy identity, or configured permission profile. Repeated runs retain their denominators, failures, and infrastructure dispositions. Comparisons identify changed harnesses, inputs, environments, or grading rules and refuse unsupported equivalence.

Prepared-trial and result-admission seams support an operator's authorized agent host without accepting arbitrary commands or requiring provider credentials for ordinary repository checks. Test doubles, deterministic conformance, replay, externally supplied live trials, and unavailable provider-backed evidence remain explicitly distinct. No live-model performance claim is made from a fixture, supplied label, or an unqualified imported score.

Reports measure elapsed time, retries, check duration, review corrections, and available tokens/cost per accepted qualified task. Unknown costs or usage never become zero, unavailable provider statistics remain explicit, resource limits are bounded, and safety or correctness failure always dominates an efficiency improvement.

A real workflow fixture records an outcome-linked defect or usability finding, adds a failing regression scenario, qualifies the correction with fresh evidence, and links passing regression coverage before feedback closes. Relevant performance/accessibility evidence is admissible with its own environment and qualification identity; unsupported user-success or production claims remain unavailable.

A future contributor starting at AGENTS.md can prepare a scoped task, run the required checks, obtain and record independent technical review, inspect ownership/recovery, prepare and grade an evaluation trial, compare qualified runs, and trace feedback to regression evidence using the canonical guide and one CLI. The lightweight path avoids requiring a multi-increment roadmap for an established local fix. The JSON-backed review site exposes current evaluation, metric and feedback summaries without revealing local authority or private run records.

The security-relevant review covers lower-trust task results and feedback, grader substitution, data minimization, model metadata, resource bounds, path and execution confinement, and integrity of aggregated metrics. Synthetic denial, failure, privacy, and exhaustion tests pass. External agents remain governed by their host permissions and operator authority; local integrity evidence is not represented as malicious-code isolation.

After both increments are implemented and change-relevant checks pass, execute npm run test:all once and applicable repository-wide documentation, agent-support, architecture, and dependency-security gates. Record raw failures and environment limits honestly, repair and rerun affected evidence where justified, validate generated roadmap artifacts, and retain the temporary report for the subsequent explicit final overall approval.

Prepared-trial manifests, protected acceptance inputs, trusted graders, repeatable run accounting, and isolated fixture execution with separately identified deterministic, replay, operator-hosted live, and unavailable evidence
Versioned privacy-minimized run manifests and comparison reports covering quality, safety, efficiency, retries, rework, environment failures, and comparability limits
Bounded feedback-to-regression records and quality-evidence references integrated with work status and completion without automatically reprioritizing product scope
Updated agent-evaluation standards, control-plane guide and CLI examples, AGENTS.md discovery checks, context routing, helper and skill documentation, and applicable provenance notices

Focused negative and end-to-end tests for real grading, grader integrity, incomparable runs, unknown measurements, unsafe imported results, feedback closure, and protection against rewarding unsafe task completion

A final concise temporary report with commands, actual outcomes, security disposition, residual risk, and honest distinction between implemented harness capability and externally measured coding-agent performance
excluded: Automatic provider/model enablement, credential collection, confidential input egress, substantial spend, or remote agent execution without existing explicit operator authority
A model leaderboard, promises of coding-agent superiority, or claiming live performance without qualified actual trials
Automatic production analytics collection, user tracking, public telemetry export, or product reprioritization from feedback
Model training, production application feature changes, unrelated UI redesign, or replacement of existing product performance and accessibility qualification
Claims of authenticated reviewer identity or hostile-code isolation that require a future approved host integration and controlled qualification

assumptions: Operator-hosted live runs remain explicitly attested; provider invocation is not automatically enabled.
Real grader execution qualifies artifacts, not authenticated identity or hostile-code containment.

plan.rollback: Disable new trial or feedback admission, preserve records and failed attempts, retain increment 1 verified delivery, and never turn unknown measurements or absent live evidence into successful results.
steps: Add five realistic task types and prepare/grade operations using bounded execution.
Add strict run metadata and comparable quality-adjusted metrics.
Add outcome-linked feedback with fail-to-pass regression proof.
Expose the new JSON summaries in the site and finish focused and overall qualification.
plan.summary: Implement prepared coding trials, executable protected graders, honest run accounting, qualified comparisons and feedback closure, then integrate their JSON review views and qualify the complete workflow.

risks: A scripted success transcript is not a grader execution or live-model evidence.
Unknown cost must not become zero, and safety failure cannot be averaged away by speed.
A trial workspace must not silently rewrite its trusted task, grader or permission profile.
Feedback closure requires observed failure, correction and fresh passing evidence.
research.summary: The current agent-support assets validate routing, not coding performance. Add isolated repository-relevant task fixtures with fixed trusted artifact graders, explicit operator-hosted live-run admission, unknown-preserving measurements and regression-linked feedback. Reuse the existing bounded execution/record primitives and expose only allowlisted JSON summaries. The security screen remains relevant for grader substitution, lower-trust artifacts, metadata privacy and resource bounds.

increments.rollback: Disable new evaluation-trial or feedback admission while preserving trial manifests, source references, grading receipts, metric reports, feedback links, and the verified delivery workflow from increment 1. Revert only additive evaluation and measurement behavior after updating routing and standards. Never fabricate a baseline, convert unknown cost to zero, erase a failed trial, weaken the independent grader, or discard regression evidence to make a comparison pass.
increments.title: Realistic agent evaluations, measured efficiency, and regression feedback
verification: During internal chunks, run only focused evaluation, run-manifest, metric-comparison, feedback, CLI, and nearest routing/skill tests.

After all increment chunks are implemented, run its change-relevant tests and public CLI fixtures, including actual failing and passing task outputs, correct abstention/escalation, grader substitution, repeated trials, unavailable measurements, incomparable runs, and feedback-to-regression closure.
Run npm run docs:check, npm run agent-support:check, and git diff --check after affected guidance and context changes.

At the overall boundary after both increments are implemented, run npm run test:all once, npm run docs:check, npm run agent-support:check, npm run architecture:check, and npm run security:dependencies when supply-chain inputs changed. Run additional builds only when the implementation affects their wiring.
Validate the roadmap state and generated artifacts; audit the AGENTS.md discovery path and all seven requested improvement areas against actual delivered evidence.
Record any missing live-provider, authenticated-review-host, dedicated performance, or platform-specific isolation evidence as outside the qualified local boundary rather than as a successful result.

workPackages.outcome: Versioned repository-relevant tasks cover a defect, a cross-boundary change, a user-facing journey, a security denial, and a correct decision-gate escalation. The harness prepares isolated work areas and executes fixed trusted graders against resulting artifacts, records actual outcomes and permitted behavior, and keeps repeated trial and environment identity comparable.
workPackages.title: Prepared coding tasks and executable acceptance grading

workPackages.outcome: The control plane records model and harness versions, instruction/context digests, duration, retries, relevant check timing, review corrections, tokens and cost when available, and approved resource limits. Reports compare time and cost per accepted qualified task, preserve missing values as unknown, and prevent efficiency scores from offsetting safety or correctness failure.
workPackages.title: Privacy-preserving run manifests and quality-adjusted comparisons

workPackages.outcome: A bounded feedback record links a defect or usability finding to the affected outcome, candidate, acceptance criterion, and regression test or evaluation case. Existing performance and accessibility qualification can be referenced where relevant, and comparison reports distinguish measured improvement, regression, insufficient evidence, and changes requiring a product decision.
workPackages.title: Feedback, quality qualification, and reusable failure scenarios
